Section 4(a) revokes Executive Order No. 12013. The order is effective August 23, 1981 under its section 8 (the signing date, August 21, 1981, is not used), and the revocation was performed when the order took effect: it is a one-time command whose object, Executive Order 12013, ceased on that date. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note 'Revokes: EO 12013, October 7, 1977' records the same effect. The revocation leaves in place the amendments that Executive Order 12013 had already made to other orders, which the Code notes still print; those are not commands of this order. The inclusive reading and the exclusive reading of the date coincide (the revocation takes effect on August 23, 1981).

clauses.reason: Section 4(b) amends section 4 of Executive Order 11961 (as amended) by deleting 'the Secretary of Commerce shall perform the functions set forth in Sections 4(a)(3) and 5(c) of the Act' and substituting 'the Secretary of Commerce shall perform the function of making periodic reports to the Committees of the Congress as set forth in Section 4(a)(3) of the Act' (before: functions under sections 4(a)(3) and 5(c); after: the reporting function under section 4(a)(3) only). Executive Order 12518 (June 3, 1985, effective on signing) later amended Executive Order 11961 (retitling it and changing section 2 and 3 wording and the Act's name) but does not touch section 4, so it is recorded as a later event on the amended order that does not change this clause. The Code prints Executive Order 11961 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12318 and 12518 (22 U.S.C. 3101 note, CURRENT:EO:12318#2) and 15 CFR part 801 cites E.O. 11961 as amended by E.O. 12318, so the amendment is embodied and the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 5 provides that the records, property, personnel and unexpended balances of appropriations relating to the functions transferred or reassigned from the Secretary of Commerce to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget are hereby transferred to the Director. The words are self-executing, so the transfer took place when the order became effective on August 23, 1981 (section 8). It is a one-time transfer exhausted by performance on that date; the transferred functions themselves continue under sections 1 to 3.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12318 of August 21, 1981 (46 FR 42833-42834; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12318.txt, read in full, location confidence high) transfers statistical policy functions from the Secretary of Commerce to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The packet marked the own-text boundary unresolved and cut the order into 14 fragments; I read the whole order (heading, eight sections, signature and the effective date of August 23, 1981 in section 8) and replaced the inventory by nine clauses: the recital, sections 1, 2, 3, 4(a), 4(b), 5, 6 and sections 7 and 8 together. Section 4(a) (revocation of Executive Order 12013) and section 5 (transfer of records and funds) are one-time commands exhausted when the order took effect on 1981-08-23; the amendments in sections 1, 2, 3 and 4(b) are embodied in the Code's printing of Executive Orders 11541, 10253, 10033 and 11961 as amended by Executive Order 12318 (CURRENT:EO:12318#4, #3, #1, #2); sections 6 and 7 are open-ended and no held source ends them. Later instruments: Executive Order 12518 (June 3, 1985; official text in the packet) amended Executive Order 11961 outside section 4, and is recorded as a later event on section 4(b); the other orders amended (11541, 10253, 10033) show no later amendment in the Code notes beyond those predating 1981 and this order. A search of the held texts for the number 12318 finds the order's copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification, and Federal Register or CFR authority lines (15 CFR part 801; 15 CFR parts cite E.O. 11961 as amended by E.O. 12318) that treat the order as in force; none amends, revokes or supersedes it. Current law: current-law:usc 8 hits (the Code notes above), current-law:ecfr 1 hit (15 CFR part 801 authority line), later-events:ofr_catalog 0 hits.
